messages:
Ben Harper: Hi everyone, first-week question: Im planning a streaming load test to validate our client library. Rough plan: ~800 streaming connections for 10 minutes from a single CI runner. Should I use sandbox or request a hosted ephemeral window? Also who do I cc for billing approval?
Lina Park: Welcome Ben! Sandbox is great for dev but streaming kernels differ a lot. For realistic latency/concurrency testing go hosted ephemeral. For 800 streams we'll need an ops ticket and billing sign-off.
Ben Harper: Thanks Lina. What's the minimum info ops wants in the ticket?
Marco Silva: Include: start/end times (UTC), total connections, expected average tokens/sec per connection, model name, whether you need IP whitelisting, and billing owner. Example: \"start 2026-04-02 15:00 UTC, duration 10m, 800 streaming connections, ~20 tokens/sec/conn, model redwood-large, source: shared-CI-NAT, billing owner: ben.manager@redwood.ai\"
Ben Harper: Perfect. Is there a quota or per-key concurrency limit I should know about? Im worried a single key will hit a cap.
Lina Park: We have per-key concurrency guards and per-project buckets. For high-concurrency streaming we often provision multiple ephemeral keys and a small routing rule. Ops can issue e.g., 4 ephemeral keys and a simple round-robin to avoid single-key bottlenecks.
Ben Harper: Nice. How can I detect I'm hitting a concurrency cap in the response? Any headers to watch?
Marco Silva: Watch response headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and when you get a 429 you get Retry-After. For streaming you might also see early connection closes; logs in Console -> Ingress will show connection errors and auth failures.
Ben Harper: Is there a recommended client behavior for streaming 429s or auth errors?
Lina Park: Exponential backoff on reconnect with jitter. For streaming reconnections we recommend base 200ms, factor 2, max 5s, but cap reconnect frequency to avoid storming. Also gracefully drain older streams on rotation.
Ben Harper: Can I check key type and expiry from CLI before running?
Marco Silva: Yes:
```
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/me | jq '.key_type, .expires_at'
```
This prints \"hosted\" or \"sandbox\" and expiry (for ephemeral keys).
Ben Harper: Any test-mode to simulate 429s so I can validate my reconnection logic?
Test Bot: Use header `X-Test-Emulate-429: after=50` to force a 429 after the 51st request on that connection. For streaming, `X-Test-Emulate-conn-close: after=10` will simulate an abrupt close. Don't use these for performance metrics.
Ben Harper: Great. About billing: will this count against onboarding credits? Who should I cc?
Priya Rao: If you're on onboarding credits, small ephemeral windows can be covered. Include billing owner in the OPS ticket. If estimate >$75 we need explicit manager approval. Ping me after filing and I can fast-track if within credits.
Ben Harper: Filing OPS-5309 now with the example text Marco provided. CCed ben.manager@redwood.ai.
ops-bot: OPS-5309 created and queued for Priya Rao.
Priya Rao: Got it. I'll review OPS-5309. If approved I'll provision 4 ephemeral hosted keys, whitelist shared-CI-NAT, and set a soft qps guard. Keys will appear in Console -> API Keys -> Ephemeral once live.
Ben Harper: Thank you! One last Q: after the run should I revoke the ephemeral keys manually?
Lina Park: They auto-expire, but best practice is to revoke them in Console -> API Keys after your test completes. Also post a short note in the ticket so ops can close it.
Ben Harper: Will do. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:
